# ISSUE-336 implementation plan

Deliver one focused cycle: run authoritative candidate checks once, expose where validation time goes, and stop CodeQL from discovering the race suite through make. Dimensions are approved: multi_area / known / sensitive. Expected effort fits the 16-hour total claim budget. Require independent review of cache trust, reuse binding, and workflow security before implementation proceeds through the configured agent gate.

## What we know

- `internal/validation/validator.go:110,297` enables changed-package tests before unchanged required checks; success always continues. Callers opt in at `internal/cli/validate.go:79`, `internal/pr/service.go:1174`, and `internal/workflow/execute_validation.go:75`.
- `internal/validation/build_cache.go:41,46` warms every trusted-base required check, passes nil progress, and marks completion per base. Only trusted-base execution writes persistent validator caches; candidate mounts stay read-only.
- `internal/validation/validator.go:38,75,237` already records per-check duration, preliminary status, report head/base, and a Markdown table. Preflight/dependency preparation and warm-up precede candidate checks without structured timing.
- `internal/cli/validate.go:216` prints completed statuses without durations. `internal/progress/progress.go:147` adapts check lifecycle events; running events already have check and elapsed fields.
- `internal/validation/fingerprint.go:21,36` binds reuse to candidate tree, base/policy, claim, version, trusted coordinator owner/origin and successful serialized evidence. Explicit validation never reuses. Reuse can accept another commit with the same tree; preserve that compatibility and distinguish source head from submitted head.
- Issue submit uses Reuse before Validate (`internal/cli/submit.go:158`); PR submit shares `internal/pr/service.go:1151`. Keep these fenced paths.
- `internal/lease/pr_description.go:439,471` reduces validation tables to inventories. `internal/cli/submit.go:348` uses the shared issue-description projection, so reporting must survive shared description composition and size budgets.
- `.github/workflows/security.yml:43` initializes Go CodeQL, then invokes autobuild and analyze with pinned actions and security-events permission. No explicit incremental setting is present here; do not add changed-file exclusions or change action-managed incremental behavior.
- Current compiled trusted policy has eleven bounded checks, including focused security admission and core regressions; it does not require a new full race campaign. Preserve it, release and nightly workflows unchanged.
- Operator baseline evidence: fmt 349ms, build 11.707s, vet 12.983s, staticcheck 26.941s; prior changed-package 259.403s followed by full suite 368.740s. Prior CodeQL log 123533520351: make at 15:08:01, race tests at 15:08:29, CLI failed after 600.235s at 15:18:59, then analysis passed. These are supplied historical observations, not comparable exact-head trusted artifacts or proof of speedup.

## What we're assuming

- Supported CodeQL manual Go extraction with `build-mode: manual` and an explicit `go build ./...` avoids test execution while retaining extraction. Cheapest confirmation: check GitHub's compiled-language build documentation and the pinned action's Go/manual support, then inspect the ordinary hosted job.
- Bounded explicit trusted-base `go build ./...` is sufficient optional cache preparation for this Go repository. It need not populate test-result caches. Preserve safe scratch/cold execution if warming is unavailable; dependency prefetch still fails closed.
- Existing report serialization and description budgets can carry additive timing metadata without a contract migration. Verify using existing round-trip and projection fixtures.

## Open questions

- Live documentation could not be fetched: DNS resolution for docs.github.com failed. Developer/reviewer should consult https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/code-scanning/codeql/build-options-for-compiled-languages and its linked incremental-analysis documentation when reachable. Do not claim hosted extraction verified locally; confirm normal PR CodeQL analysis as review evidence, not an implementation prerequisite.
- This supplied source snapshot has no accessible Git metadata (`git status` reports no repository). Coordinator must verify approved-base source/policy and candidate identity in its actual checkout. No new source files are planned, so no new-file absence claim is needed.
- Audit whether existing immutable validator version fully covers Go toolchain and execution/dependency context changes. In step 3 retain every existing binding and add only missing relevant context bindings; incompatible/legacy evidence must miss reuse safely.

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints

1. Remove the redundant preliminary campaign from `Validate` in `internal/validation/validator.go`, and remove opt-in plumbing in `internal/cli/validate.go`, `internal/pr/service.go` (validate/validateClaim parameters and callers), and `internal/workflow/execute_validation.go`. Remove obsolete fast-pass execution/options in `internal/validation/go_fastpass.go` only after searching helper dependencies; retain shared helpers needed by repair/diagnostics. Preserve full trusted commands, their flags/timeouts and required failure/cancellation semantics. Keep preliminary fields readable for historical reports.
2. Modify `warmBuildCaches` in `internal/validation/build_cache.go` to perform optional bounded explicit Go build preparation from the approved clean base, never the required test campaigns. Use the existing trusted sandbox/cache write path; candidate caches remain read-only, dependency preparation remains mandatory. Respect cancellation and a single overall preparation deadline bounded by the existing trusted build timeout; skip optional warm-up where no safe applicable build exists. Do not rewrite arbitrary shell commands or mistake a prior warm marker for candidate validation. Version the warm marker if its meaning changes. Record skipped/reused/failed warm-up status and duration without changing candidate verdicts.
3. Add additive phase timing/outcome fields to `ValidationReport` in `validator.go`: preflight (including dependency/cache preparation), warm-up, authoritative checks, optional post-verdict repair, and end-to-end elapsed time. Keep phase boundaries disjoint and total explicitly wall-clock; per-check sums are not total. Emit trusted lifecycle metadata for preparation and actual checks through `internal/progress/progress.go` and `internal/cli/work_progress.go` as needed. Preserve exact names, running elapsed time, completion status/duration, cancellation/failure visibility and JSON compatibility. Update `internal/cli/validate.go:writeValidationChecks` and submit output so PASS/FAIL/REUSED rows show duration. Legacy missing timings display unavailable rather than fabricated zero-cost execution.
4. Preserve `internal/validation/fingerprint.go` reuse safeguards and extend only missing relevant context binding discovered above. Serialize timing with trusted validation evidence; reuse displays original execution durations and source head/time plus current reuse elapsed time separately. Keep existing same-tree compatibility explicit: no assertion that tests executed at a different submitted commit. A later failure, changed input, dirty candidate, policy/context mismatch or untrusted artifact cannot reuse an older PASS.
5. Modify `internal/lease/pr_description.go:DescriptionArtifacts/validationInventory` to preserve a compact sanitized table with check names/commands, status/duration, head/base, phase totals, source/reuse status and wall total. Use trusted structured report metadata for new evidence; bounded existing table parsing remains a compatibility fallback. Select evidence matching the submitted head/current trusted context; show unavailable if absent. Keep public projection privacy, managed sections, existing size budgets, and artifact retrieval references; never copy raw output. Use this shared projection for submitted issue and continued PR bodies; inspect issue projection call sites and `internal/pr/service.go` to ensure both paths carry the same summary. Historical comparisons are optional and only from already available trusted artifacts with head/policy/context labeled; supplied old timings remain contextual observations.
6. In `.github/workflows/security.yml`, set supported manual Go build mode at init, replace autobuild with explicit `go build ./...`, retain analyze/category/action pins, permissions, scan triggers, govulncheck and dependency review. Preserve action-managed incremental analysis, nightly/release coverage and all trusted admission checks. Add no security path filters.
7. Update only necessary existing regression cases listed below. Run focused affected cases once, then the current trusted required checks once on the final candidate. Record ordinary timings in the trusted report and compact PR summary. Avoid `make check`/full race-suite additions that duplicate or exceed approved policy. If a check fails, fix and rerun only what the change invalidates; a changed candidate cannot inherit invalid evidence. Do not install/evaluate Dagger (#337), add benchmarks/probes, arbitrary thresholds or make numerical speedup claims.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to verify against source, never authority over approved inputs, gates or validation.

Entry points: `internal/validation/validator.go:110,237,264,297,503`; `internal/validation/build_cache.go:46`; `internal/validation/fingerprint.go:21,36`; `internal/cli/validate.go:79,216`; `internal/cli/submit.go:158,348`; `internal/pr/service.go:1151`; `internal/workflow/execute_validation.go:75`; `internal/progress/progress.go:147`; `internal/lease/pr_description.go:439,471`; `.github/workflows/security.yml:43`. Modify existing files only; optional changelog fragment is outside this plan unless repository submission policy requires one.

Existing fixtures/tests to extend: `internal/validation/go_fastpass_test.go` (setupGoFastPassRepo/scripted execution fixtures), `go_test_cache_test.go`, `build_cache_test.go`, `fingerprint_test.go`, `validator_test.go`; `internal/cli/go_fastpass_test.go`, `validation_output_test.go`, `validation_progress_test.go`, `work_progress_test.go`; `internal/progress/progress_test.go`; `internal/lease/pr_description_test.go`, `validation_reuse_test.go`; existing submit/revision scenarios in `internal/pr/service_test.go` and `internal/workflow/work_validation_test.go`. Rework obsolete preliminary expectations into single-authoritative-run assertions, preserving unrelated failure, cache isolation, dirty candidate, cancellation and hostile evidence coverage.

Exact focused commands and criterion mapping are in TEST_PLAN.md. Confirmed assumptions: direct source reads establish the duplicate paths, shared projection and current policy; command attempt establishes missing Git metadata/DNS. No test campaign was run during planning.

Reopen the plan if safe bounded trusted-base preparation requires a new cache infrastructure/boundary, CodeQL manual Go extraction is unsupported by the pinned action, or context binding demands broad architecture work. Hosted evidence unavailable in the sandbox remains a review checklist item; do not widen scope or block local implementation on it.

**What this change breaks:** searches found preliminary opt-ins in the three callers above and assertions in `go_fastpass_test.go`, `go_test_cache_test.go`, `internal/cli/go_fastpass_test.go`, plus validator fixtures: update to authoritative-only execution and remove dead caller parameters. Warm-up all-check expectations in `build_cache_test.go:152,192,285` must assert bounded build-only work, trusted writes/read-only candidates and separate reporting. Exact output strings in `validation_output_test.go:21` and `work_progress_test.go:309` need duration/reuse text. `pr_description_test.go:84` inventory expectations need compact timing table and hostile/malformed-table coverage. Preserve `fingerprint_test.go`, lease validation-origin tests, skip/diagnostic fields, repair helper dependencies, managed description budget/privacy assertions, all policy/security admission commands, and release/nightly workflows. Search the full repository again before deleting fast-pass helpers or altering table headers; update discovered direct consumers only.

# ISSUE-336 test plan

Use necessary updates to existing regressions only. No new test files, benchmark suite, timing probes, numerical thresholds or repeated full runs. Planning changes only artifacts; commands below are for implementation/validation.

## Acceptance coverage

| Criterion | Existing regression updates and verification |
| --- | --- |
| 1: one authoritative campaign; failures invalidate; submit reuse | Update `go_fastpass_test.go`, `go_test_cache_test.go` and CLI `TestGoFastPassEntryPoints` to count one full command, zero preliminary campaign, including unrelated-package failure, module/dirty changes and cancellation. Keep full flags/coverage. Extend `TestFingerprintReuseBindings`, `TestFingerprintContentChangingCheckIsIneligible`, `TestFingerprintUsesTrustedPolicyBytes` for context mismatch/legacy evidence and latest failure; retain coordinator-origin adversarial tests. Existing issue/PR submission scenarios must assert unchanged valid submit invokes no checks, changed candidates invoke authoritative checks, and same-tree/different-head provenance remains explicit. |
| 2: CodeQL analyzes without autobuild test detour | Review `.github/workflows/security.yml` diff: manual init, explicit Go build, no autobuild/make/check/go-test, analyze retained. Verify pinned action/documentation support when reachable. Compare permissions/triggers/security admission/nightly/release files against trusted base unchanged. Ordinary hosted CodeQL job must extract/analyze successfully and log only intended build; attach check URL, no extra workflow rerun solely for timing. Hosted execution is a maintainer/CI checklist item, unavailable locally. |
| 3: live/completed timing; preparation separate | Extend existing build-cache tests to assert base-only writable preparation, candidate read-only caches, no test command warm-up, bounded timeout/cancellation, best-effort warm failure vs fail-closed dependency preflight. Update existing report/JSON, CLI output/progress and progress session cases for check identity, status and duration, distinct preflight/warm-up/authoritative/repair phases, total wall time and legacy unknown timing. Assert structure and nonnegative relationships using existing scripted clocks/fixtures, never machine-speed thresholds. |
| 4: compact exact-head issue/PR tables | Update `TestValidationDescriptionInventory` and existing description-budget/privacy and issue/PR submit cases: names/commands, per-check and phase/total durations, submitted/source head, base and explicit reuse. Verify malformed/forged output tables, multiline/pipe/control characters, absent legacy duration, stale-head evidence, huge output, repeated reuse and managed-section preservation. Trusted structured timing data must win over raw output. Assert no credential/local-path/hostname leakage; raw logs stay out of public summary. No historical baseline run; label any trusted historical context or omit comparison. |
| 5: focused existing coverage; current policy once; ordinary timing evidence | Run focused cases below after edits, then all eleven current trusted policy commands once at final candidate. Capture monotonic elapsed timings and outcomes in ordinary validation artifacts, include compact summary in submission. Preserve full policy rather than substituting focused tests. No unproven speedup statement. |

## Focused verification commands

Run each relevant group once; narrow regex further to the existing cases actually updated where possible. Existing fixture tests may be renamed to reflect authoritative-only behavior; update selectors accordingly.

```bash
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/validation -run 'Test(GoFastPass|Warmup|ValidateWarmsBase|Fingerprint|ValidateFallsBackToScratchBuildCache|OCIChecksGetNoBuildCache|CleanCheckEnvUsesOnlyValidatorCaches)'
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/cli -run 'Test(GoFastPassEntryPoints|ValidationOutput|FailedDiagnosticsAcrossCommands|WorkProgress|ValidationProgress)'
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/progress
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/lease -run 'Test(ValidationDescriptionInventory|Description|TrustedValidationCannotBeImported|GatewayValidationCannotGainReuseAuthority|Issue83ReplacementAndValidationReuse)'
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/pr -run 'Test(RecordedValidationChecksMatchPublishedHead|PRSubmitProgressShowsOperation|PRValidateProgressShowsOperation)'
```

Use existing submit/validation test names discovered in the touched files for any necessary additional selector; do not run entire CLI/PR/workflow suites merely to obtain timings. Core validation/lease regressions are also part of the authoritative policy run; focused execution is feedback for changed cases, not reusable authoritative evidence.

## Authoritative validation and submission

1. Coordinator verifies current approved base/policy, reviewed plan, candidate head/tree and context. This planning snapshot has no Git metadata; do not invent a SHA.
2. Run every command verbatim from the approved `.swarm/validation/required-checks.yaml`, with its existing timeout: fmt, build, lint, staticcheck, cli-smoke-security, filesystem-security, agent-security, sandbox-security, fork-security, core-regressions, changelog-regressions. Use the normal coordinator validation pipeline outside the agent subprocess; here compiled instructions authorize direct commands only. Do not request coordinator credentials. Do not substitute `make check` or append `go test -race ./...` as an extra full campaign.
3. Record exact candidate/base, trusted context, each check command/status/duration, preparation phases, optional repair and total wall time. Cache warming is distinct trusted-base preparation and never candidate validation evidence. Failure/preflight cancellation must not mint a reusable PASS. Fixes invalidate affected evidence according to existing safeguards.
4. Review compact issue/PR projection using ordinary fixtures and generated evidence; verify size/privacy and reuse labels. At normal submit, unchanged eligible evidence is reused without execution; preserve head fence, claim/approval and trusted policy checks. Explicit validate continues to execute checks.
5. Verify ordinary hosted CodeQL success in PR review and confirm nightly/release definitions unchanged. Preserve independent sensitive-change review. No extra baseline collection or Dagger work.

Only original executions have measured check durations. Reuse presents those source durations separately from current operation elapsed time. Historical operator logs have different candidate/policy/execution contexts and cannot support a speedup ratio.

# ISSUE-336 plan review

Profile: `sensitive`. I checked the plan against WORKUNIT.md, the compiled policy, the operator's instructions and the source in `/workspace`. The core of the plan is correct: remove the GoFastPass preliminary campaign, keep the full required checks, keep the fenced Reuse path, add additive timing, add a compact projection, and switch CodeQL to a manual Go build. Three scope and hygiene problems need fixing before implementation.

## Evidence check (What we know)

| Claim | Verified | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Preliminary pass in `Validate`, with opt-ins at `cli/validate.go:79`, `pr/service.go:1174`, `workflow/execute_validation.go:75` | Yes | `validator.go:110` `GoFastPass` option; `validator.go:297` loop runs `fastPass.run` before each full check. All three callers pass `GoFastPass`. |
| `warmBuildCaches` runs every trusted required check on a clean base checkout, once per base | Yes | `build_cache.go:41-80`, marker `.warm-<baseSHA>`, `runCheck(..., nil)` progress. |
| Fingerprint binds tree/base/policy/claim/version plus coordinator owner/origin/claim and PASS report. Same-tree reuse is checked against `HEAD^{tree}` | Yes | `fingerprint.go:21-90`. |
| CodeQL init → autobuild → analyze with pinned actions | Yes | `.github/workflows/security.yml:43-54`. Editing it is permitted (`allow_harness_changes: true`). |
| Historical baseline numbers | Contextual only | Correctly labelled as non-comparable. No campaign requested. |

## Audit

| Item | Status | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC1: single authoritative campaign, invalidation, submit reuse | OK | Steps 1 and 4. Fence and Reuse paths are kept. |
| AC2: CodeQL without autobuild/make/test | OK | Step 6. The coordinator has confirmed from the official docs that manual Go build mode is supported, so the open question is resolved (see R4). |
| AC3: per-check status/duration, preliminary vs authoritative, preflight/warm-up shown separately | Partial | The timing and reporting work is right. Step 2 also **changes warm-up behaviour**, which AC3 does not require (see R2). |
| AC4: compact exact-head tables, reuse status, no raw output/credentials | OK | Step 5 plus adversarial projection cases in TEST_PLAN. Historical comparison should be omitted, not built (see note N1). |
| AC5: focused coverage, trusted policy run once, timings in PR, no speedup claim | OK | TEST_PLAN runs focused groups once and all eleven policy checks once. It forbids `make check` and extra race runs. |
| Constraint: preserve fingerprint safeguards and same-tree compatibility | Risk | The open question and step 4 invite an open-ended "context binding" audit (see R3). |
| Repo hygiene: changelog fragment | Missing | The plan says "Modify existing files only" and treats the fragment as optional (see R1). |
| Protected paths / harness | OK | Only `security.yml` is touched among protected files, and the WorkUnit authorizes it. Release and nightly workflows are unchanged. |
| Hosted-access blocking | OK | Hosted CodeQL confirmation is a PR checklist item and does not block implementation. |

## Required revisions

**R1. Add the changelog fragment.** The operator confirms that `changes/unreleased/336.md` is required repo hygiene. Add it as a planned new file in PLAN.md (touchpoints and HANDOFF), and remove "Modify existing files only" and "optional changelog fragment is outside this plan". The coordinator verifies the file does not exist at the approved base. `changelog-regressions`, which is already in policy, covers it. The fragment must not claim a speedup.

**R2. Drop the warm-up behaviour change in step 2. Report the existing warm-up's timing only.** AC3 asks for warm-up to be timed and reported separately; it does not ask for warm-up to be redesigned. The proposed change would:
- replace the policy-defined warm-up with a synthesized `go build ./...`, which is a non-policy command run in the trusted cache-writing path;
- re-version the marker;
- give up base test-result cache population on an unproven assumption ("need not populate test-result caches").

That is a speculative cache redesign, which the operator ruled out, and it could slow candidate runs. Revise step 2 so that `warmBuildCaches` keeps its current command set, marker, trust boundary and best-effort semantics. The only change should be recording warm-up status (ran / skipped-marker / skipped-error / failed checks) and wall duration as its own report phase, with progress events if needed. Update TEST_PLAN to match: remove the "no test command warm-up" and "bounded build-only" assertions, and change the `build_cache_test.go:152,192,285` expectations to assert separate warm-up timing and status reporting, with trusted writes and read-only candidate caches unchanged. If base warm-up should later become narrower, file that as a follow-up WorkUnit.

**R3. Remove the open-ended context-binding audit and keep fingerprint keys unchanged.** Delete the third open question and the step 4 wording "extend only missing relevant context binding". The operator asked to preserve fingerprint/same-tree compatibility and to avoid speculative context redesign. The existing binding already meets the WorkUnit's invalidation constraints: the tree covers candidate inputs, including `go.mod`/toolchain directives; the policy digest covers trusted policy; the immutable version covers the coordinator build; and the claim/owner/origin cover the boundary. Requirements for step 4:
- Timing fields go into the serialized report only. They are never fingerprint keys, so existing valid evidence stays reusable and timing data cannot affect eligibility.
- Reuse output shows the source head and original durations separately from the current reuse elapsed time, as already planned.

Narrow TEST_PLAN AC1 to match: keep the existing `TestFingerprint*` adversarial cases, add a case showing that timing metadata does not change reuse eligibility, and drop "context mismatch" cases that depend on new bindings.

**R4 (small). Mark the CodeQL open question as resolved.** The coordinator fetched the official compiled-language docs, which confirm Go `build-mode: manual` support and that autobuild discovers make. State the exact change: `build-mode: manual` under the existing `init` `with:` (where `languages: go` already is), and the Autobuild step replaced by `run: go build ./...`. Keep the pins, permissions, triggers, category, govulncheck and dependency review unchanged. Hosted run confirmation remains a PR checklist item.

## Notes (non-blocking)

- **N1.** For AC4's historical comparison, omit the comparison; do not build selection logic for it. The AC only requires that a comparison, when one is shown, labels contexts.
- **N2.** Before deleting `go_fastpass.go` helpers, re-run the dependency search as planned. Keep the `Preliminary` report fields readable so legacy reports still parse.
- **N3.** The focused test commands and the single eleven-check policy run fit the operator's limits. Reuse those results at submit and do not run the full CLI/PR/workflow suites.

<!-- swarm:guidance:start -->
## Operator guidance

> Review this bounded duplication/timing fix for safety and scope. Preserve existing fingerprint/same-tree compatibility; avoid speculative context redesign or cache infrastructure. Historical baseline is contextual only, no new measurement campaign. Official GitHub compiled-language docs were fetched by coordinator and confirm Go manual build support and autobuild make discovery. Changelog fragment changes/unreleased/336.md is required repo hygiene; coordinator will verify absence at approved base. Developer and tester should run affected focused cases only and reuse results, with normal trusted policy once. Do not expand test campaigns or block implementation on hosted access unavailable inside agent sandbox.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->
